intro:
Checking the gold price in Sri Lanka today is an essential routine for families shopping for wedding jewellery, savers protecting household wealth, and buyers comparing rates along Sea Street in Colombo, Kandy, Jaffna, and Galle. Because gold ornaments serve both as treasured cultural heirlooms and an instant source of financial liquidity across the island, tracking the live Sri Lanka gold rate today in Sri Lankan rupees (LKR) helps you make informed decisions before visiting a showroom.

Our live tables above display the current gold rate in Sri Lanka per sovereign (pawn / 8 grams) and per 1 gram for 24K and 22K purities, accompanied by a detailed price-by-weight table, an interactive calculator, and live silver prices. In this guide, we explain how the Sri Lankan pawn (sovereign) weight system works, why Sea Street (Chettiar Street) rates differ from showroom invoices, how 22K and 24K purities compare, and how to evaluate making charges and buyback terms.

sections.h2: Gold Price in Sri Lanka Today: Reading Live Rates in Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR)
paragraphs: When you check the gold price in Sri Lanka today in the live table at the top of this page, you are viewing real-time spot-derived benchmarks converted directly into Sri Lankan rupees (LKR). While international bullion markets quote wholesale gold in US dollars per troy ounce, Sri Lankan jewellers and households universally measure and price gold using two everyday units: the sovereign—widely called a pawn or pound locally, equal to 8 grams—and the metric 1 gram rate.

Our live pricing table separates 24K pure bullion from 22K jewellery gold so buyers can immediately compare raw investment metal against the standard purity used for necklaces, bangles, and rings. Because global commodity exchanges and currency markets trade continuously throughout the business week, the LKR figures in our table adjust automatically to reflect live international momentum.

It is important to note that the figures shown in the live table represent the intrinsic spot value of the metal before local import tariffs, showroom overheads, and craftsmanship charges are added. Before visiting Colombo's Pettah gold market or a national jewellery chain, you can enter your desired weight in grams or sovereigns into our calculator above to establish a fair baseline.

sections.h2: Understanding the Sovereign (Pawn / Pound) and Gram Weights in Sri Lanka
paragraphs: In Sri Lanka, the cornerstone unit of retail gold trade is the sovereign, which locals across Sinhala, Tamil, and English conversations commonly refer to as a pawn or a gold pound (pavan in Tamil). In modern Sri Lankan jewellery trade, one pawn or sovereign is standardised at exactly 8 grams of gold. Whenever families discuss the budget for a bridal necklace, a thali / kurukku, or a set of bangles, the quantity is almost always counted in pawns—such as a half-pawn ring (4 grams), a one-pawn chain (8 grams), or a five-pawn necklace.

While shoppers speak in pawns, every registered showroom in Sri Lanka weighs ornaments on calibrated electronic scales in metric grams and milligrams. Because one pawn equals 8 grams, converting between the two units is straightforward: simply multiply the 1 gram gold rate by eight to verify the 1 sovereign (8 grams) price shown in our live table above.

For larger bullion transactions or international comparisons, our price-by-weight table also lists standard metric increments including 10 grams, 20 grams, 1 troy ounce (31.1 grams), 50 grams, and 100 grams. Keeping the 8 grams pawn relationship clearly in mind ensures you never confuse a Sri Lankan 8-gram pawn quote with the 10-gram benchmark used in parts of India or the 11.66-gram tola used in Northern South Asia.
bullets: 1 Sovereign / Pawn / Pound: Standardized at exactly 8 grams in Sri Lankan jewellery trade.
Half Pawn (4 grams) and Quarter Pawn (2 grams): Everyday fractional benchmarks for rings, pendants, and earrings.
1 Gram: The metric unit used on computerized showroom scales for exact billing.
10 Grams and 1 Ounce (31.1 grams): Useful reference weights for bullion bars and cross-border comparisons.

sections.h2: 24K vs 22K Gold Purity in Sri Lanka: Which Should You Buy?
paragraphs: Sri Lankan gold buyers primarily choose between two purity grades: 24K and 22K, with 18K playing a supporting role for gemstone settings. At the top of the purity chart is 24K gold (stamped 999 fineness), which consists of pure unalloyed gold. Because 24 carat metal is naturally soft and malleable, it is unsuitable for intricate clasp work or daily-wear rings; instead, Sri Lankan buyers purchase 24K in the form of investment biscuits, small bullion bars, and pure coins.

For virtually all traditional and bridal jewellery in Sri Lanka, 22K gold—universally identified by its 916 hallmark stamp—is the undisputed island-wide standard. By alloying twenty-two parts pure gold with two parts copper, silver, or zinc, goldsmiths achieve a durable, resilient metal that holds intricate Kandyan bridal designs, traditional Tamil thali chains, and modern machine-cut bangles while preserving a rich, unmistakable golden glow. Consequently, the 22k gold price in Sri Lanka today is the benchmark most shoppers track daily.

When purchasing jewellery set with natural sapphires, rubies, diamonds, or semi-precious Ceylon stones, buyers also encounter 18K gold (stamped 750 fineness). Because 18 carat gold contains a higher proportion of strengthening alloy, its prongs grip precious gemstones much more securely than softer 22K metal.
bullets: 24K (999 fineness): Pure unalloyed gold reserved for investment biscuits, coins, and bullion wafers.
22K (916 fineness): The premier Sri Lankan standard for bridal necklaces, thali chains, bangles, and rings.
18K (750 fineness): Durable alloy ideal for jewellery mounted with Ceylon sapphires, diamonds, and gemstones.
Always inspect the inner band or clasp of any ornament for the 916 or 750 fineness hallmark.

sections.h2: Colombo Sea Street (Chettiar Street) vs Branded Jewellery Showrooms
paragraphs: Anyone researching the gold rate in Sri Lanka quickly encounters two distinct pricing tiers: the wholesale-oriented Pettah / Sea Street (Chettiar Street) bazaar rate in Colombo and the retail tariff quoted by major branded showrooms across the island. Sea Street has served for generations as Sri Lanka's central bullion and jewellery artery, housing dozens of closely packed shops and wholesale dealers where high turnover keeps spreads tight.

Because Sea Street dealers compete intensely on volume and often quote separate base rates for 24K biscuits and 22K pawn weights before adding negotiated craftsmanship fees, their headline per-pawn quotes frequently sit slightly below those of luxury air-conditioned malls. By contrast, large national jewellery chains invest heavily in multi-branch security, accredited gemmological testing laboratories, hallmark certification guarantees, and structured lifetime exchange policies, which are reflected in their showroom pricing.

Regardless of whether you shop along Sea Street in Colombo, in Kandy's city centre, or in Jaffna's Stanley Road and Kasturiar Road jewellery district, checking the live spot-derived 24K and 22K rates in our table above gives you an objective anchor before you begin comparing quotes.

sections.h2: Why Final Jewellery Prices Differ: Making Charges, Wastage, and Taxes
paragraphs: When you select a 22K necklace or pair of bangles in a Sri Lankan showroom, the final invoice is always higher than the simple multiplication of the item's weight by the live 22K per-gram or per-pawn rate. This difference comes from making charges (craftsmanship labour) and wastage allowances added by the jeweller to cover the cost of transforming raw bullion into finished ornaments.

Simple machine-manufactured chains, plain wedding bands, or stamped coins carry relatively low making charges per pawn. Conversely, intricate handcrafted Kandyan bridal sets (such as the traditional seven-necklace mala set), elaborate Tamil bridal harams, or antique filigree designs require extensive artisan labour and solder work, commanding higher craftsmanship fees. Additionally, national import duties, Value Added Tax (VAT), and social security levies applicable to commercial jewellery businesses influence retail showroom spreads.

If you are buying jewellery set with Ceylon sapphires, cubic zirconia, or pearls, always ask the salesperson to weigh or specify the net gold weight separately from the stone weight. Paying the 22K gold price on heavy synthetic stones is one of the most common costly mistakes shoppers can easily avoid.

Handcrafted Kandyan and Tamil bridal ornaments carry higher artisan labour fees than basic machine chains.

sections.h2: What Moves the Gold Price in Sri Lanka: LKR Exchange Rate, Economy, and Festivals
paragraphs: Two primary economic forces drive the daily Sri Lanka gold rate today: the international US dollar spot price of bullion and the exchange rate of the Sri Lankan rupee (LKR) against the US dollar. Because Sri Lanka imports its bullion requirements and global gold trades in US currency, any depreciation or appreciation of the LKR immediately alters the local per-pawn price. During periods when the Sri Lankan rupee strengthens, local gold prices can ease even if global spot gold holds steady; conversely, rupee weakness rapidly pushes domestic pawn prices upward.

Gold also plays a unique role in household banking across Sri Lanka through the widespread practice of gold pawning (ranahana / gold-backed micro-loans) offered by commercial banks and licensed finance companies. Because families know that 22K hallmarked jewellery can be pledged at any bank branch for immediate working capital, rural agricultural needs, or emergency funds, physical 22K gold enjoys constant island-wide demand.

Cultural and religious seasons further shape showroom activity. The Sinhala and Tamil New Year (Aluth Avurudu / Puthandu) in April, the Thai Pongal harvest festival, Deepavali, Akshaya Tritiya, and auspicious wedding seasons (nekath / muhurtham dates) generate strong retail buying across every province.
bullets: LKR-to-USD currency exchange rate shifts directly and immediately impact local pawn and gram prices.
Global spot bullion movements driven by central banks and inflation set the international baseline.
Widespread bank gold-pawning facilities make 22K jewellery a highly liquid household financial asset in Sri Lanka.

sections.h2: Smart Buying, Pawning, and Hallmarking Tips for Sri Lankan Shoppers
paragraphs: To get the best value when buying gold in Sri Lanka, always prioritize certified purity and transparent documentation. Look for the 916 hallmark laser-stamped on 22K jewellery and the National Gem and Jewellery Authority (NGJA) certified assay marks where available. Many reputable showrooms in Colombo and major towns can also verify karat purity in seconds using non-destructive electronic XRF karatmeters right at the counter.

If you are buying gold partly as a financial safety net that might be pledged for a bank pawning advance or exchanged in the future, stick to solid 22K (916) chains, bangles, or 24K coins without heavy stone settings or hollow wax-filled interiors. Commercial banks value pledged ornaments strictly on the net pure gold content after deducting stone weight and testing karatage, so solid 916 pieces always secure the highest valuation.

Finally, always collect a detailed official invoice listing the exact metric weight in grams (alongside the pawn equivalent), the guaranteed karat purity (22K / 916 or 24K / 999), the separate making charge, and the showroom's specific buyback and exchange terms.

faq.q: How many grams are in 1 sovereign (pawn / pound) of gold in Sri Lanka?
faq.a: In Sri Lanka, 1 sovereign—commonly called a pawn or a gold pound—equals exactly 8 grams of gold. A half-pawn equals 4 grams, and a quarter-pawn equals 2 grams, all of which can be calculated directly from the 1 gram and 8 grams rows in our live table above.

faq.q: What is the difference between 24K and 22K gold in Sri Lanka?
faq.a: 24K gold (999 fineness) is pure unalloyed metal sold mainly as investment biscuits and coins, whereas 22K gold (916 fineness) blends twenty-two parts pure gold with two parts alloy to create strong, durable jewellery for weddings and daily wear.

faq.q: Why do Sea Street gold prices in Colombo differ from branded showrooms?
faq.a: Sea Street (Chettiar Street) in Pettah operates as a high-volume wholesale and bazaar hub with lower retail overhead and negotiable making charges, whereas branded national showrooms factor in multi-branch security, certified lab testing, and formal exchange guarantees.

faq.q: How does the Sri Lankan rupee (LKR) exchange rate affect local gold prices?
faq.a: Because international bullion trades in US dollars, any change in the LKR-to-USD exchange rate directly changes the local rupee cost of importing gold. Even if global gold prices stay flat, a weaker rupee pushes Sri Lankan pawn rates higher, while a stronger rupee brings them down.

faq.q: Why does a 22K necklace cost more in a shop than the live 22K gold rate?
faq.a: The live table displays the intrinsic metal value of 22K gold. Retail jewellers add making charges (artisan labour), wastage allowances for handcrafted designs, any gemstone costs, and applicable local taxes to calculate the final showroom price.

faq.q: Which gold purity is best for bank pawning or investment in Sri Lanka?
faq.a: For pure investment, 24K (999) coins and biscuits carry the lowest fabrication markup. For jewellery that doubles as a liquid asset for bank pawning advances, solid 22K (916) chains and bangles without stones offer the highest net-gold valuation.

faq.q: How can I verify that my 22K gold jewellery is genuine in Sri Lanka?
faq.a: Inspect the piece for the 916 fineness stamp, ask the jeweller for a non-destructive electronic XRF karatmeter test slip or National Gem and Jewellery Authority assay mark, and ensure the 22K guarantee is written on your official receipt.
